This doesn't feel like the correct mapping to me.. Do we need to ask Redfish to add a new property??

Gunnar discussed with Redfish about adding an Extended Version property to the schema a while back, that's the reason we started populating the D-Bus property by default: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openbmc/+/56271

I agree with Gunnar that SoftwareId ("The implementation-specific label that identifies this software.") doesn't really fit with Extended Version ("The xyz.openbmc_project.Software.ExtendedVersion interface can be added to any Software.Version to express the versioning of the aggregation.").
SoftwareId can be seen more like a hash of the version string, like the "version id".

I'd suggest like Gunnar mentioned to follow-up with Redfish to add an "Extended Version" property to the schema. At that time Redfish was not opposed to the idea but did not see a use-case for it, so perhaps now showing them the smbios example they'll be willing to add it.

Smbios exposes `FirmwareID` as part of Type 45 record. 
We mapped `FirmwareId` to extended version instead of creating new property under Version Dbus interface. 
Here is the MR https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/78934 which was abandoned where the dbus repo owners suggested to use ExtendedVersion instead of creating new dbus property

The SoftwareID can also be used for showing Component Identifier in the Firmware Inventory.

I also don't think it should be mapped to Extended Version.

We should either add a new property in Version Interface or create a new interface with SoftwareID property.
Yes, will float an PDI MR for SoftwareId. Once that is there will work on bmcweb MR for adding SoftwareId property

It's not really helpful for one repository to do this random different thing than everywhere else though and then expect bmcweb to handle it.  We should get this added to the software-update design if we're expecting this to be general and/or optional practice.

The bad thing about what's been done here is that we now have code using some dbus object for software that isn't intended for software and there are a lot of fields that clearly are not being filled in by smbios-mdr.  So now, the properties are just ... blank?  People seem to forget that dbus properties aren't "optional".
